status: Public author contract and manually reasoned examples frozen before candidate implementation; independent parent receiving remains separate.

model.input: Two well-formed JavaScript strings of 0–24 Unicode code points each; reject nonstrings and lone UTF-16 surrogates. No trim, case folding, or normalization.
model.excluded_operation: Adjacent transposition is not one edit.
model.matrix: D[i][j] is minimum source-prefix i to target-prefix j cost. Row 0 is j; column 0 is i. Interior is min(diagonal + equality/substitution cost, above + deletion cost, left + insertion cost).
model.ties: Every optimal predecessor is retained. Canonical backtrace, starting at D[m][n], chooses diagonal first, then deletion, then insertion; reverse the chosen steps for forward alignment.
model.counts: Exact BigInt internally; decimal strings in the returned/downloaded record. Count optimal monotone alignment paths, not distinct final strings or arbitrarily reordered edit programs.

result.cell: {i,j,cost,optimalPathCount,candidates:[{operation,from:[i,j],stepCost,totalCost,optimal}]} in deterministic diagonal/delete/insert order; origin has no candidates.
result.alignment_step: {step,operation,sourceIndex,targetIndex,source,target,cost,from:[i,j],to:[i,j]}; zero-based source/target indices or null at a gap; step is one-based; origin-to-final order.

ui.entry: Directly opened, dependency-free single HTML file.
controls: Edit both source and target; explicitly Compare.
Select any prefix cell by button or arrow-key movement to inspect candidate costs and all ties.
Previous/Next/Show all canonical-alignment steps; no automatic motion.
Explicit download of the exact applied comparison JSON, with policy/input/matrix/candidates/path/alignment.
Separate fixed 14-question course JSON download for the unchanged learner.
ui.draft: Keep literal draft text. Mark retained results as previous when inputs differ. Disable comparison download until a valid comparison matches the draft. A failed comparison does not publish a new result.
ui.representation: Use DOM text nodes for all inputs, including markup, quotes, whitespace and Unicode. Show indices and code point labels; a gap is explicitly labeled and not an ordinary text character.
ui.phone: No page-level horizontal overflow at 320px; dense prefix matrix may scroll within its own labeled region.
ui.network: No external dependency, storage, account or runtime fetch; reference hyperlinks are user initiated.

course.basis: Original questions, worked guide and explanations. Native parser, adaptive selection, review/practice and study-note export remain unchanged.

receiving.baseline: Exact original source closure and representative native deck/learner/review flow before candidate; no new feature exists in baseline.
receiving.author_math: Frozen manual cases plus independent exhaustive enumeration of all monotone alignment paths for every pair of binary strings of length <=4; verify both minimum cost and number of minima, and replay selected alignment.
receiving.browser: Actual installed Chromium interaction and physical downloads, including import into exact unchanged learner, one mixed-answer session and practice/notes; private profile, no account or remote page.
receiving.preservation: Exact before/after source pins, first failures and artifacts. No unrelated source writes; source publication and parent receiving distinct.

references.title: Wagner and Fischer (1974), The String-to-String Correction Problem
Levenshtein (1966 translation), Binary Codes Capable of Correcting Deletions, Insertions, and Reversals
Unicode UAX #29, revision 49, grapheme cluster boundaries

manual_examples.note: Path count deliberately not frozen from an unproved mental calculation.
Canonical alignment inserts U+0065, then substitutes U+00E9 with U+0301.
Three source code points: U+1F469, U+200D, U+1F52C.

refusal_examples.reason: Lone high surrogate is not admitted.
Lone low surrogate is not admitted.

Invalid UTF-16 examples are represented here by numeric code-unit arrays for native construction; no candidate code existed.
